newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh launches rescue effort after cyclone.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh launches rescue effort after cyclone.

text.p: Bangladesh launched a massive rescue and relief operation on Tuesday in areas devastated by a severe cyclone that local newpapers said had killed hundreds of people.
Army, naval and police units joined thousands of volunteers and fanned out across coastal regions in the southeast of the country, officials said.

"But detailed estimates of losses of lives and property will not be available soon as many areas are still cut off after more than 200 kph (124 mph) winds, accompanied by rain, pounded the coast and offshore islands," said Golam Rabbani, director of Cyclone Preparedness Centre in Chittagong.
The Bangladesh Times, a government-run daily, reported on Tuesday that up to 500 people were feared killed in the cyclone, which tapered off by midnight on Monday.
Other newspapers, quoting their own sources, put the death toll at more than 350. More than 2,000 people were injured in the main port city of Chittagong alone, they said.
Some 250 others had been killed in Cox's Bazar, one of the areas worst hit by the cyclone, the newspapers said.
About 100 fishermen from the coastal district of Patuakhali were missing at sea, newspaper reporters in Chittagong said.
Officials last night confirmed nine deaths and more than 100 injured, and said the figures would rise.
The cyclone, roaring in from the Bay of Bengal, ravaged Chittagong, the Cox's Bazar and Tenkaf districts and several islands, leaving a trail of devastation.
Rescue and relief operations were hampered overnight by darkness and rough weather, relief ministry officials said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was expected to visit the devastated areas on Tuesday, her aides said. Earlier she cancelled a planned visit to Spain in the wake of the cyclone.
Tens of thousands of houses were demolished and uprooted trees and power poles jammed roads in the worst affected areas. Power supplies and communications were cut in many places.
Chittagong port had suffered substantial damage, port officials said without giving details.
They said the fate of the Panamanian flag ship Esco Argo, which sent an SOS message during the cyclone saying it was sinking in the Bay of Bengal near Kutubdia island, was still not unclear.
